relevance_note: Case report of two siblings with Majeed syndrome carrying a homozygous LPIN2 variant: "In both patients, a homozygous single-base pair change in the donor splice site of exon 17 of the LPIN2 gene".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. Scope: two affected siblings (Case 1, Case 2), their mother (tested, heterozygous), a second-degree cousin labelled #20 in the pedigree (diagnosed with MS in infancy, previously published as ref 6), and two pairs of previously published siblings from the Discussion (ref 7: onset ages; ref 9: features and treatment stated for both siblings as a named group). Not given rows: the father (DNA not available, not tested, not described as affected); Family A/Family B and ref 10 variants (families/variants only, no individual described); the 'child with MS' of ref 15 (no individual-level fact beyond diagnosis and treatment response). No variant rows for #20, ref 7 or ref 9 people: the Discussion lists variants by reference but never ties one unambiguously to a person (the ref 9 sentence is garbled). The Markdown prints '>' as '>' and the transcript as 'NM\_014646.2'; spans keep the Markdown text, values give the printed characters (c.2327+1G>C, NM_014646.2). Transcript is the reference sequence stated for the LPIN2 analysis; the protein p.Arg776SerfsTer66 comes from the Discussion sentence naming this exact variant (c.2327+1G>C). Inheritance for the homozygous siblings is 'inherited maternal' because the mother is stated heterozygous for the same variant; the father was not tested. Consanguinity for Case 2 is from the statement that Case 1's parents (her parents) were first-degree cousins. CRMO is left 'not reported' for Case 1 and Case 2: the paper calls their disease chronic osteomyelitis / nonbacterial osteomyelitis, never recurrent multifocal; these are recorded as features. Lab values without a stated interpretation (Case 1 HB 9.3 g/dL, Case 2 HB 7.7 gm/dL, serum iron) are recorded as observed values, not mapped to anemia; Case 2 'anemia' is stated. Case 1 serum iron 7 umol/L is within the printed normal range but not called normal, so not recorded. Case 1 differential (polymorph 7%) not mapped to neutropenia. D-27 normal-finding rows: 'Physical examination, including musculoskeletal system, was unremarkable' (Case 1) and 'Urine and stool analysis were normal' are whole examinations; recorded as written and they exclude nothing more specific. Case 2 swelling was absent at the first examination and present two months later (right ankle); treated as a change over time, not a contradiction, so the checklist item is observed. Case 1 joint swellings at presentation versus an unremarkable musculoskeletal examination: possible tension, recorded both, checklist observed from the history. Case 1 CRP is printed as 70 mg/dL (normal <3) while later values are in mg/L; recorded as printed. Figure 5 legend (Case 2's smear and marrow) used as paper text. Chronic osteomyelitis and CDA for both siblings come from the sentence naming 'both siblings'. Ref 9 siblings: the paper does not name their diagnosis explicitly (context is MS treatment), so disease_label is not reported.
